newsitem.title: CANADA: Winter storm blamed for three deaths in Quebec.
newsitem.headline: Winter storm blamed for three deaths in Quebec.

text.p: A winter storm of freezing rain and blowing snow that hit the Canadian province of Quebec on Friday and Saturday is being blamed for the deaths of three young people.
The bodies of a 20-year-old man and a 15-year-old girl who were reported missing in a snowstorm near the provincial capital of Quebec City on Friday night were found on Sunday morning, police said.
A 17-year-old youth who had accompanied the two was found alive and remained in critical condition in a Quebec City hospital.

Provincial police said the trio had been dropped off by snowmobile about 328 feet (100 metres) from a cottage on L'ile d'Orleans, an island in the St. Lawrence River on Friday night. They appeared to have become disoriented in the snowstorm and did not reach the cottage, police said. They were eventually found after a search that included a police helicopter, volunteer snowmobilers and a dog team.

The body of another man, 21, was found on Sunday in his car parked along a highway south of Quebec City. The man's car was found after being lightly struck by a snowplow clearing the road, police said.
The snowstorm dumped about 19.7 inches (50 cm) of snow in the Quebec City area, 170 miles (275 km) northeast of Montreal along the St. Lawrence.

Elsewhere in the province, freezing rain and high winds disrupted power for about 193,000 customers of Hydro-Quebec, the province electrical utility. By Sunday, power had been restored to almost all of the households affected.

Quebec provincial police said no fatal highway accidents were reported in the province during the storm. In Ontario, Canada's most populated province, the weekend storm was blamed for hazardous driving conditions that caused seven highway deaths.
